title: BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave) - Band 20 (800 MHz) for GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Takeshi Yamamoto

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave) filter targeting Band 20 (800 MHz) for GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter. The filter is designed on Langasite substrate with a target center frequency of 1671.9 MHz and bandwidth of 32.6 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave)
- Frequency Band: Band 20 (800 MHz)
- Application: GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter
- Substrate: Langasite
- Package: Fan-Out WLP
- Design Tool: Keysight ADS 2024
- Design Center: Cedar Rapids Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave) design targeting Band 20 (800 MHz). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       1671.9 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       32.6 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 2.2 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 18.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 40.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 36.0 dB
Q Factor:               2253
Temperature Coefficient:-6.7 ppm/°C
Die Size:               1.9 x 2.2 mm
Wafer Size:             8-inch
Number of Resonators:   4
Electrode Material:     Al
Passivation:            SiO2
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Keysight ADS 2024 and load the BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave) template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: Langasite with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 1671.9 MHz, BW 32.6 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 2.2 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (Fan-Out WLP).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (8-inch, Langasite).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Keysight E5080B ENA.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 5016 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 2.2 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 18.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 49 MHz offset >= 40.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 7 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 1.4 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +33 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 500 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 92%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2025-03-22
Devices Tested:         53
Insertion Loss (meas):  1.89 dB
Return Loss (meas):     20.5 dB
Rejection (meas):       43.1 dB
Isolation (meas):       41.4 dB
Q Factor (meas):        2253
Group Delay Variation:  2.6 ns
Power Handling:         +30 dBm
Die Yield:              85.2%

Result Classification:  FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The BAW (Bulk Acoustic Wave) design demonstrated below-target performance for Band 20 (800 MHz).
b) Insertion loss met target specification.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Temperature stability was within specification across full range.
e) No delamination observed after 1000-cycle thermal shock test.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Optimize resonator geometry to reduce insertion loss by ~0.3 dB.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Escalate to advanced materials team for alternative piezoelectric stack.
